findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)' (TA-metricator-hec-for-nmon), not a Cisco ACI add-on. The same wrong ID is repeated in dataSources, references and detailedImplementation (and the Step 5 troubleshooting tells readers to check 4022 compatibility matrices).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the current Cisco ACI collection path (the cached catalogue says the old ACI add-on 1897 is deprecated in favour of Cisco DC Networking, Splunkbase 7777) and correct every 4022 mention.

findings.explanation: The cached Splunkbase catalogue lists 'Splunk Add-on for VMware' (splunk_TA_vmware) as app 3215; 1810 is not that add-on. The wrong ID recurs in dataSources, references and detailedImplementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Splunkbase 3215 for the Splunk Add-on for VMware throughout.

findings.explanation: 4856 is not in the cached catalogue, and the only cached NSX add-on is 'VMware NSX add-on' (TA-nsx, 6805), a syslog CIM-mapping add-on with no cluster-status API input.
findings.suggested_fix: Look up Splunkbase 4856 and confirm its name and whether it polls NSX Manager cluster status; otherwise state that cluster status is collected via REST API Modular Input (1546) against the NSX cluster API.

findings.explanation: None of these sourcetypes appear in the category guide's sourcetype inventory (which uses cisco:aci:health/fault, vmware:nsxt:*, cisco:ndfc:event), yet app/detailedImplementation present them as outputs of named add-ons. The NSX one also uses the vmware:nsx: prefix while the guide uses vmware:nsxt:.
findings.quote: **`cisco:aci:cluster_health`** (APIC Raft/VIP semantics with degraded or split-brain text); **`vmware:nsx:cluster_status`** (NSX Manager three-node cluster plus VIP health); **`cisco:ndfc:cluster`**
findings.suggested_fix: Label these as custom sourcetypes produced by REST collectors you define, or switch to the sourcetypes the referenced add-ons actually emit.

findings.explanation: APIC clustering is documented as sharded data with replicas distributed across controllers, not Raft; the 'APIC Raft tolerates a single missing controller' anchor repeats this.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Cisco APIC Getting Started / cluster management guide and describe the actual shard/replica and quorum behaviour.

findings.explanation: The SPL copy in detailedImplementation differs from the spl field (which uses the `.` concatenation operator), and `concat()` is not a documented Splunk eval function, so the pasted copy is likely to fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Paste the spl field verbatim so both copies match.

findings.explanation: The SPL is a raw sourcetype search and uses none of these models; Inventory describes host/asset inventory and Performance host resource metrics, neither of which models controller-cluster leader/quorum state, and the 'schema' text is speculative.
findings.suggested_fix: Set cimModels to [] or justify one model with the field mapping that would populate it; drop the speculative schema/dataModelAcceleration text.

findings.explanation: The URL is the Cisco.com home page, not the MIM reference; the Splunkbase 4022 and 1810 reference titles are also wrong (see app finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Link the actual APIC Management Information Model reference page and fix the Splunkbase reference titles/IDs.

findings.explanation: maint_suppress only suppresses leader_gap in the SPL; the drill text suggests the opposite expectation and does not say which score component should still fire. Alert design also uses earliest=-45m@m while the SPL hardcodes earliest=-24h@h.
findings.quote: **Drills** — With maint_suppress true, scores should rise, then fall when steady state returns.
findings.suggested_fix: State that maint_suppress=true suppresses only the leader_gap (55) tier while degraded/split tiers still fire, and note the alert overrides the time range.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by an automated reviewer while carrying wrong Splunkbase IDs and invented TA sourcetypes.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME validates against real APIC/NSX/NDFC data.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: In `ha_risk_score=case(...)` the branch `syslog_ha_signal==1 AND degraded_ctrl==1,45` is unreachable because `degraded_ctrl==1,70` is evaluated first and case() returns the first true condition; the advertised 45-point 'syslog-corroborated degradation' tier never occurs, and syslog-only HA signals (degraded_ctrl==0) score 0 and are filtered out.
After `bin _time span=15m`, earliest(_time)/latest(_time) return the bin start, so first_hit = last_hit and last_hit_human shows the bin boundary, not the last event time.

summary: A thoughtful multi-platform controller-HA design with useful validation and troubleshooting notes, but the add-on attributions are wrong (Splunkbase 4022 is an Nmon add-on, Splunk Add-on for VMware is 3215 not 1810), the TA-specific sourcetypes appear invented, the 45-point risk tier is unreachable, and the CIM mapping is decorative.
